title: Shared spend shelving and GPU-family shadow pools for soft budget caps
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Customers run inference across regions and heterogeneous accelerator types. Current hard budget gates are causing unnecessary request failures or heavy SLA violations when spot pools saturate. We need a soft, tenant-scoped spending control that preserves SLOs while enforcing spend ceilings and preferring cheaper capacity when available.

Proposal: Implement a "shelving" layer in the routing stack that maintains per-tenant spend windows and a shadow pool map of GPU-family preferences. The shelving layer will: 1) track rolling spend against a configurable cap, 2) apply score penalties to routes that exceed preferred spend bands, 3) surface a shadow-pool of lower-cost compatible instance families for graceful fallback, and 4) allow configurable soft-throttle behavior (queueing, shed-to-degraded-variant, or degrade-to-on-demand at reduced concurrency) rather than immediate hard rejections.

Goals: reduce hard rejects due to budget exhaustion, reduce tail latency regressions from aggressive fallbacks, and provide predictable unit-costs for tenants while maximizing overall utilization of spot/preemptible capacity.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant spend window recorded and queryable via /admin/spend API
Routing layer applies dynamic penalty multiplier when tenant spend exceeds soft-cap threshold
Shadow-pool mapping exists for at least 3 GPU families and includes compatible model variant mapping
No customer-facing 5xx increase >2% for impacted tenants during staged rollout
Integration test that simulates spot reclamation shows shelving switches to degrade-to-variant within 150ms median decision time
technical_notes: Architecture: shelving layer lives between the allocator and router decision surface; it accepts per-request metadata (tenant_id, model_id, cost_estimate, priority) and returns route_score penalties and fallback hints.
State: use a sharded in-memory window per-tenant (ring buffer of 1-minute buckets) with eventual persistence to Redis for durable counters. Keep precision to token-cost granularity.
Shadow-pool: static baseline mapping plus runtime telemetry-driven adjustments. Start with families: A100-40GB, A10G, and T4-equivalent (quantized variants).
Policy knobs: soft_cap_pct, panic_cap_pct, penalty_curve (linear|exp), backlog_behavior (queue|shed|degrade), variant_degrade_priority
API: admin endpoints to inspect tenant spend, override caps, and pin shadow-pool preferences for enterprise tenants.
Telemetry: expose metrics spend_window_used_ratio, penalty_applied_count, fallback_hint_rate, decision_latency_ms. Hook into existing Console dashboards and alerts.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (P0): Implement per-tenant in-memory spend window + admin read API
Phase 2 (P1): Integrate penalty multiplier into router scoring and add simple shadow-pool hints
Phase 3 (P2): Implement degrade-to-variant orchestration and queueing fallback
Phase 4 (P3): Telemetry dashboards, canary rollout, and runtime knob UI in Console
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Incorrect spend estimation for batched requests could misfire penalties. Mitigation: add conservative rounding up and include token pre-estimates from runtime before dispatch.
Risk: Shadow-pool variant may not match quality requirements for some tenants. Mitigation: per-tenant allowlist for variants; fallback to on-demand when pinned.
Risk: Additional decision latency. Mitigation: keep shelving decision under 1ms via in-process cache and only fall back to Redis for updates every 10s.
Risk: Gaming the soft-cap by splitting tenants. Mitigation: aggregate by billing account and allow cross-tenant enforcement for linked sub-accounts.
test_plan: Unit tests for spend window math and penalty application
Load tests simulating 10k QPS with mixed spot reclaim events
Fault-injection test for Redis failover and shelving degraded mode
End-to-end canary with three enterprise tenants on dedicated capacity and gradual traffic ramp
rollout_steps: Deploy shelving as opt-in feature flag for 5 pilot tenants
Monitor metrics for 48 hours with rollback criteria (5xx spike >2% or avg latency +20%)
Enable default soft-cap for free-tier tenants only, evaluate cost and stability
Progressively enable for standard tenants with conservative caps and provide self-serve override in Console
